Here's a regex for an ISO 8601 calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`):

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` matches the four-digit year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` matches the month, 01–12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` matches the day, 01–31.
- `^…$` anchors the match to the whole string. Drop the anchors, or use `\b` instead, to find dates inside longer text.

It matches `2026-10-01` but rejects `2026-13-01` and `2026-10-32`.

It checks the format, not the calendar. `2026-02-31` still matches, so validate the actual date in code if you need that.
